narrowings: decay.kind loses the value `multiplicative`. Mandated by ADR-001 section 8 item 3 on measured grounds (ADR-001:328-336). Costs nothing: no file in Exported/Characters/ uses it, `decay.ratio` is retained so a stale ratio still validates, and json_spec.py does not consult this schema, so the ban is enforced by validation and by the adapter's load assertion A02 rather than by the loader. THIS IS THE ONLY THING v2 CAN EXPRESS LESS OF THAN v1.
relaxations: engine.schema_version goes from `const: 1` to `enum: [1, 2]`. Without this no v1 file could validate against v2 and the superset claim would be false on its most trivial field.
x-v2-changes.renames: None. No [P] field is renamed, retyped, or given a new default. v1's `certain`, `caveat`, `engine.hit_condition` (string), `cancel_rules` and `cancel_families` all survive verbatim, including the two redundant spellings v1 said should be reduced to one -- reducing them would break a shipped file for no gain.

x-migration.what_a_v1_file_must_change_to_become_a_v: NOTHING. A v1 file IS a v2 file. This is the intended answer and it is measured, not argued: all three files in Exported/Characters/ validate against schema.v2.json unmodified, and their three verdicts are byte-identical before and after. See x-v2-verification.
x-migration.the_one_thing_worth_checking: If a file authored `decay.kind: "multiplicative"` it now fails VALIDATION (though it would still LOAD, because json_spec.py never validates). No file in this repository does. Convert it to `table` with integer permille multipliers, which is D8's preferred escape, and re-measure -- do not convert it to `linear` by eye, because ADR-001:338-355 shows what inventing a decay rule does to a character that has none.
optional_uplift_when_a_file_is_next_touc: Set engine.schema_version to 2 to assert the author knew about the nine fields. Nothing keys off it.
Move engine.hit_condition's prose into the structured move.hit_condition, leaving the prose as provenance. Kung Fu Girl has 17 of these.
Move cancel.engine.condition's prose into the structured predicateList. AOF2 has 26, all identical, so authoring it once on a cancel_families entry is the intended shape.
Set escape_hatch.closed_by on every hatch the new data actually closes. This is what turns ADR-001:522-524's re-measurement into a query instead of a re-read.
Author engine.variants on aof2_strength_training.json, whose 10 moves already carry engine.variant integers with nothing to point at.
x-migration.what_migration_does_NOT_mean: Adding the nine fields' DATA to the three characters is Phase 3, not migration. A schema that can hold the data and a file that holds it are different deliverables, and ADR-001:98-100 is explicit that the second one is Phase 3's. escape_hatch.needed stays true until the data is written.

x-known-over-approximations.$comment: ADR-001 names three halves that a schema field cannot close, and rule 3 of this work item requires each to be documented as a bounded over-approximation with its DIRECTION stated. ADR-001:224-225 fixes the vocabulary: the permissive direction 'can invent an infinite but cannot hide one' and is safe; the other direction hides infinites and is a soundness bug. TWO OF THE THREE ERR SAFE. ONE DOES NOT, and it is named as a soundness bug below rather than softened.

min_reach.closable_half: The ENGINE half is closed by move.engine.min_reach_sub + input.proximity_variant. The engine knows the threshold and picks the right state.
min_reach.unclosable_half: The PROVER half. move.reach expresses a MAXIMUM gap because model.py:473-476 emits a `__space >= max_reach - reach` guard and __space is max_reach - gap (model.py:495-497). A MINIMUM gap is an upper bound on a resource, and the fragment's only comparison is componentwise >= (comboprover.hpp:256-262). There is no encoding.
min_reach.direction: PERMISSIVE -- SAFE. The model lets the attacker use a far normal point-blank, granting a move the real character would replace with its close variant. It can invent an infinite; it cannot hide one.
min_reach.bound: Confined to the 8 moves in 2 characters that carry a proximity_variant. On Kung Fu Girl the pair is stand_hk_far/stand_hk_close (corpus/kfg/Kung Fu Girl.cmd:802) and the over-credit is at most the difference between the two moves' frame data.
min_reach.partially_closable_after_all: The CLOSER member's constraint IS expressible today and ADR-001 does not say so. stand_hk_close is selected only at gap <= 15 px and `reach` is exactly an upper bound on the gap, so authoring reach 0.15 instead of the 0.52 taken from its Clsn1 box would encode the selector exactly and remain sound. Not done here because reach is [P] and the change must be re-measured; offered to Phase 3.

projectile_contact_frame.closable_half: The ENGINE half is closed by move.engine.projectile: spawn tick, velocity, lifetime and the projectile's own hit profile are all now expressible.
projectile_contact_frame.unclosable_half: The PROVER half. Move.startup is a constant; a fireball's frame of contact is a function of distance. 'Startup 15' means only 'released on frame 15'. VERIFIED against the corpus: Kung Fu Man's hasyo has startup 15, and the Projectile controller fires on animelem=10 of anim 1100 (corpus/kfm/kfma4a_cns.txt:2429), whose first tick is 15 (corpus/kfm/kfma4a.air:1448 and the nine elements before it). The two coincide exactly, which is the point -- startup measures release, not contact.
projectile_contact_frame.direction: CONSERVATIVE -- THIS IS THE DANGEROUS ONE, AND IT IS A SOUNDNESS BUG, NOT A SAFE APPROXIMATION. Reasoning: the prover measures hitstun from the moment the move connects and measures every cancel delay from that same moment. A projectile's authored delay is derived from the attacker's own animation and is therefore measured from RELEASE, while in reality the defender's hitstun begins at CONTACT, which is f ticks later. The model therefore starts and ends the defender's hitstun f ticks too early while the attacker's follow-up availability is unchanged, so the model credits the attacker with LESS frame advantage than reality gives. Less advantage means a loop the real character can perform may be reported dead. That HIDES an infinite, which ADR-001:224-225 and :369-374 both classify as the unacceptable direction -- it is the same failure the rejected `meter_room` design was rejected for.
projectile_contact_frame.bound_and_why_the_phase_0_verdicts_are_u: MEASURED, not argued: hasyo and suiten_hasyo have ZERO outgoing cancels in kung_fu_man.json (8 and 5 incoming, 0 outgoing each). The under-credited advantage is the advantage AFTER a projectile connects, and no edge in any of the three files consumes it. The unsoundness is therefore real, latent, and inert across the entire Phase-0 corpus, and Kung Fu Man's TERMINATING verdict does not rest on it.
projectile_contact_frame.what_would_close_it: Not a schema field. Either a distance-dependent startup in the fragment -- which is a new Move shape, not a new key -- or, cheaply and soundly, authoring a projectile move's outgoing cancel delays as if contact were at the minimum plausible range, which over-credits the attacker and flips the direction to the safe one. Phase 3 must do the second before authoring the first such edge, and this note exists so that it is a decision rather than an accident.

defender_has_no_state.adr_001: section 4 group G, :266-268 -- the part of G that no field closes
defender_has_no_state.closable_half: The two predicate halves are closed as DATA by move.hit_condition and cancel.engine.condition, and ADR-001 section 8 item 5 makes Phase 5's trigger language responsible for making them prover-visible.
defender_has_no_state.unclosable_half: 'Defender state as an outcome.' AOF2's sweep sets fall = 1 with fall.recovertime = 12 (corpus/aof2/States.st:419-421): the combo ends because the defender enters knockdown, not because frame advantage ran out. 'comboprover has no state for the defender at all.' A predicate language over the defender does not help, because there is no defender for it to be about; this is a property of the fragment, and no v2 field and no Phase 5 grammar closes it.
defender_has_no_state.direction: PERMISSIVE -- SAFE. The prover ignores knockdown, so it lets a combo continue past a hit that really ends it. It can invent an infinite; it cannot hide one.
defender_has_no_state.bound: Every move whose reaction sets causes_knockdown. Recorded per move in engine.reaction.causes_knockdown / fall_recover_ticks, which v1 already carries.

x-known-over-approximations.and_the_ones_that_are_not_over_approxima: Distinct from the three above and not fixed by any schema. ADR-001:486-497 names two quantities that are estimates rather than approximations: PUSHBACK, which MUGEN never records as a displacement and which a +-20% error flips the midscreen verdict on (ADR-001:390-404), and HITSTUN DECAY, which MUGEN does not have at all. Both are authored numbers with a stated rule, not schema limits, and ADR-001:508-510 names deriving pushback from an instrumented Ikemen GO build as the single most valuable measurement not yet taken.

x-load-assertions.$comment: Rules that JSON Schema draft 2020-12 cannot express, because each compares one part of the document to another or one file to another. They are listed here with ids so the adapter can implement them and cite them, exactly as v1 made the v2 backlog queryable rather than prose. ADR-001 section 8 item 3 explicitly asks for the decay pair to be 'asserted at load'. STATUS: A01-A04 are verified against all three shipped files in x-v2-verification.

A01.why: max(floor, base - step*n) means a floor above a base RAISES it and invents frame advantage (model.py:260, comboprover.hpp:81)

A02.why: repeated float multiply then truncate, reproducible by neither integer kernel

A03.rule: every character in a build declares the same resources in the same order
A03.why: comboprover::Character keys a ResourceVec by INDEX (comboprover.hpp:56, :128-129, :152), so a mismatch silently compares meter against juggle

A04.rule: no MOVE effect/guard map and no CANCEL effect/guard map authors the key `__space`. Gap actions are exempt and MUST be able to author it
A04.why: On a move the prover MERGES rather than honours an authored value -- model.py:476 does guard[SPACE] = max(authored, need) and :479 does effect[SPACE] = authored - units(pushback) -- so an authored number silently combines with a derived one and the file no longer says what it appears to say. On a GAP ACTION the opposite is true: authoring `__space` is the only way to express displacement, and it is the documented mechanism ('walking forward is simply a positive effect on the distance resource', gap.py:54-56). model.py:510 APPENDS a synthesized `walk` action alongside the authored list rather than colliding with it.
A04.scope_correction: An earlier draft of this assertion said 'no effect or guard map' unqualified, and its `why` claimed a collision with model.py:495-497. Both were wrong. Executed as written it rejects all three Phase-0 characters -- kung_fu_girl and kung_fu_man author {__space: 0} on gap_action `microdash`, aof2 authors {__space: 170} on `run_close` -- and two of this schema's own worked examples. It was authored from reasoning and never run against the corpus, which is the same defect class as the `derivation_legend` type error and the A06 over-fire recorded below. Verified before and after: 3 of 3 characters violate the old wording, 0 of 3 violate this one.

A05.why: the [P] scalars must be the first hit, because every cancel delay is measured from first contact

A06.rule: consider only the UNCONDITIONAL hit records, i.e. those with no `condition`. If the last of those has a hitstun_ticks differing from hits[0]'s, then engine.hits_projection_caveat must be present and must name the direction
A06.why: the projection is then an approximation whose direction depends on the numbers, and the conservative direction hides infinites
A06.applies_when: engine.hits has more than one unconditional entry
A06.why_conditional_records_are_excluded: A record carrying a `condition` is an ALTERNATIVE profile, not a sequel -- Kung Fu Girl's chop registers its second HitDef only when the first WHIFFED (corpus/kfg/Normal.cns:224), so the two are mutually exclusive and the second is never 'the last hit of the combo'. An earlier draft of this assertion omitted the exclusion and fired on chop, which is how the distinction was found: it flagged a 30-vs-33 hitstun difference between two hits that can never both land. Counting an alternative as a sequel would also credit the attacker with 198 damage from one button.

A08.rule: motion[].tick strictly increasing, and every velocity an integer
A08.why: ARCHITECTURE.md:47 -- the authoritative core is int32 sub-units

A09.why: for a projectile move, startup means release and nothing else (ADR-001:246-247)

A10.rule: a transition with kind on_land must carry duration_bound and duration_derivation
A10.why: move.recovery is then an approximation and only the author knows its direction; a default would let the infinite-hiding direction ship silently

A11.rule: if any gap action declares a non-null engine.variant, then engine.variants.prover_reading must be present and notes[] must carry the union warning
A11.why: the prover sees the union of all variants, so an INFINITE verdict may name a route no single sub-character can perform

A12.rule: every [P] field has a sibling engine.derivation entry naming a file:line or saying ESTIMATED in capitals
A12.note: v1's stated rule, unchanged; warning rather than error because derivation_defaults legitimately covers most moves

A13.rule: move.engine.min_reach_sub is set only on a move whose engine.input.proximity_variant.selects is this_when_farther
A13.why: they are the same fact written twice; the closer member has a maximum, not a minimum

x-worked-examples.$comment: One complete worked example per new field, every one drawn from a citation ADR-001 section 4 actually makes, and every corpus line re-read at the cited line for this schema rather than carried over. Tick numbers are computed from the .air element durations and agree with the [P] startup already shipped in each character file. THESE ARE EXAMPLES, NOT TRANSCRIPTIONS -- writing them into the three characters is Phase 3 (ADR-001:98-100).

motion.adr_001: section 4 group B, :206-213 -- 'e.g. palm at Specials.cns:29-46 (PosAdd x=3 at AnimElem 2, VelSet x=5.5 across elements 3-5, VelMul x=.8 as friction, VelSet x=0 at element 6)'
motion.corpus: corpus/kfg/Specials.cns:29-32 (PosAdd), :34-37 (VelSet), :39-42 (VelMul), :44-47 (VelSet 0); ticks from corpus/kfg/Kung Fu Girl.air:1693-1725
motion.derivation: AnimElem 2 begins tick 3, AnimElem 3 begins tick 6, AnimElem 6 begins tick 14 (element durations 2,3,3,2,3,4 from .air:1693 onward). MUGEN runs controllers in file order each tick, so from tick 6 to tick 13 VelSet x=5.5 at :34-37 runs and then VelMul x=.8 at :39-42 runs, giving a CONSTANT 4.4 px/tick, not a decaying one. At tick 14 the VelSet x=5.5 trigger has expired, VelMul takes 4.4 to 3.52, and VelSet x=0 at :44-47 then zeroes it. Resolved: 3 px teleport at tick 3, 4.4 px/tick for ticks 6-13, 0 from tick 14. Total forward travel 3 + 8*4.4 = 38.2 px.
motion.quantization: 4.4 px/tick * 256 = 1126.4, authored as 1126 sub-units (4.3984 px). The loss is 0.0016 px/tick over 8 ticks = 0.0125 px total. DIRECTION: the attacker travels very slightly LESS far, which under-states attacker mobility -- it can hide an infinite, not invent one, the same safe direction as the walk_speed hole ADR-001:499-504 documents. This is exactly the class of loss ADR-001 means by 'no loader ever rounds is not fully achievable'.

hits.adr_001: section 4 group A, :191-192 -- 'KFM f_lk_cancel, state 275: two HitDefs at animelem=4 and animelem=10 (kfma4a_cns.txt:767-884). Transcribed with the first only, which is what mugen_cns.py:530-535 does.'
hits.derivation: anim 275's first eight elements last 1 tick each, so AnimElem 4 begins tick 4 -- which is the [P] startup already shipped -- and element 9 lasts 12 ticks, so AnimElem 10 begins tick 21. HitDef 1: damage 20 (:788), ground.hittime 23 (:798), ground.slidetime 12 (:797), ground.velocity -3 (:799). HitDef 2: damage 30 (:819), ground.hittime 23 (:829), ground.slidetime 16 (:828), ground.velocity -3 (:830). Meter: statedef poweradd 20 (:774) plus getpower 20 (:803) = 40 MUGEN power = 4 units, which is the [P] effect.meter already shipped.
hits.note: BOTH HitDefs author ground.hittime = 23, so hits_projection `first` is EXACT for this move and assertion A06 does not fire. That is worth stating because it is luck, not design: the file's own transcription_note says the second hit is dropped, and it happens to be dropped without cost to the frame data.

hits_alternative_profile.field: move.engine.hits[].condition (a hitRecord that is an ALTERNATIVE, not a sequel)
hits_alternative_profile.adr_001: section 4 group A, :198-200 -- 'KFG chop: a SECOND HIT PROFILE selected by whether the first whiffed -- near at AnimElem 4 (Normal.cns:185-220), far at AnimElem 5 gated on triggerall = !movecontact && !movereversed (Normal.cns:223-225), with different damage, hitstun and reach.'
hits_alternative_profile.corpus: corpus/kfg/Normal.cns:184-220 (Hit 1) and :222-258 (Hit 2); ticks from corpus/kfg/Kung Fu Girl.air:800-820
hits_alternative_profile.derivation: anim 211 elements last 4,4,5,3,4..., so AnimElem 4 begins tick 14 (the [P] startup) and AnimElem 5 begins tick 17. Hit 1: damage 102 (:192), ground.hittime 30 (:208), ground.velocity 0 (:211). Hit 2: damage 96 (:231), ground.hittime 33 (:246), ground.velocity -9 (:249), and its box is longer (.air:816 per the character file's own escape-hatch note).
hits_alternative_profile.note: This is the one hitRecord in the corpus that needs a `condition`. It is NOT a second hit of a combo -- the two are mutually exclusive, and the second exists only because the first whiffed. Modelling it as a sequel would credit the attacker with 198 damage from one button. The prover still sees exactly one Move; the alternative profile is engine-only.
hits_alternative_profile.note_on_assertion_A06: A06 deliberately does NOT fire here even though the two records differ in hitstun (30 vs 33), because the second carries a `condition` and A06 considers only unconditional records. This example is how that exclusion was found: a draft of A06 without it flagged chop, and the flag was wrong -- the two hits can never both land, so the second is not 'the hitstun the combo leaves'.

hits_summed_damage.adr_001: section 4 group A, :196-197 -- 'KFG super_palm: three HitDefs (Supers.cns:82 firing at AnimElem 5 and 13, :105 at AnimElem 21) collapsed into one record whose damage is their sum, 219.'
hits_summed_damage.corpus: corpus/kfg/Supers.cns:81-102 (one HitDef with trigger1 = AnimElem 5 at :83 and trigger2 = AnimElem 13 at :84) and :104-112 (AnimElem 21 at :106); ticks from corpus/kfg/Kung Fu Girl.air:2465-2557
hits_summed_damage.derivation: anim 3000: AnimElem 5 begins tick 11 (the [P] startup), AnimElem 13 begins tick 37, AnimElem 21 begins tick 62. Damage 72 (:87) fires twice and 75 (:109) once: 72+72+75 = 219, which is the [P] damage already shipped. ground.hittime is 32 on all three (:97 for the first two, :119 for the third), so assertion A06 does not fire and the `first` half of this projection is exact.
hits_summed_damage.note: The first two hits are ONE HitDef with two triggers, which is why hits[] is keyed on tick rather than on source controller. Summing into [P] damage is safe because json_spec.py:69 sends damage to Result.maxDamage only and never to the verdict; nothing else is summed.
hits_summed_damage.note_on_the_third_hit: The third HitDef also carries `fall = 1` (corpus/kfg/Supers.cns:125): the super ends in a knockdown. That is an instance of x-known-over-approximations.defender_has_no_state -- the prover has no defender state, so it does not know the combo has ended, and it will happily continue past this hit. Permissive, therefore safe, but it is why this move's outgoing edges deserve a second look in Phase 3.

proximity_variant_and_min_reach.adr_001: section 4 group C, :216-217 -- 'value = 250 + (Abs(P2BodyDist X) <= 15) * 1 (Kung Fu Girl.cmd:802 [V], same idiom at :774 and :756-family)'
proximity_variant_and_min_reach.derivation: The ChangeState value is 250 plus 1 when Abs(P2BodyDist X) <= 15, so state 251 (close) is selected at a gap of 0-15 px and state 250 (far) at 16 px and beyond. min_reach_sub for the far member is 16 * 256 = 4096. Note ADR-001 section 7 records that the working notes cited :804 for this line and the verified line is :802; :802 is what was re-read here.
proximity_variant_and_min_reach.note: Both members carry the object, each naming the other. Only the FAR member carries min_reach_sub (assertion A13) -- the close member's constraint is a MAXIMUM, and a maximum on the gap is the one thing `reach` already expresses. See x-known-over-approximations.min_reach.partially_closable_after_all.

projectile.adr_001: section 4 group F, :244-245 -- 'KFM hasyo and suiten_hasyo attack via a Projectile controller, not a HitDef (kfma4a_cns.txt:2338-2477)'
projectile.derivation: The Projectile controller triggers on animelem=10 (:2429). anim 1100's element 5 lasts 6 ticks and the rest 1 each, so AnimElem 10 begins tick 15 -- exactly the [P] startup already shipped, which is the measured form of ADR-001:246's 'startup 15 means only released on frame 15'. All the ifelse(var(5),...) parameters take the LIGHT branch, because ADR-001:298 records that only the light set is transcribed: velocity 3.2 (:2438), projremove 98 (:2436), damage 80 (:2440). Offset 26,-70 (:2437). ground.hittime 21 (:2451), ground.velocity -9 (:2453).
projectile.quantization: 3.2 px/tick * 256 = 819.2, authored as 819 sub-units (3.1992 px/tick). NOT EXACT: 3.2 = 16/5 and 5 does not divide 256. Over the 98-tick lifetime the fireball falls 0.78 px short of its float trajectory. This is engine-only -- the prover models no projectile at all -- so it cannot move a verdict, but it is a real divergence between the engine and MUGEN and belongs in engine.fit.known_losses when this move is re-transcribed.

projectile.quantization_note: velocity 3.2 px/tick is 819.2 sub-units and is authored as 819; see x-worked-examples.projectile.quantization

on_land.adr_001: section 4 group D, :229-230 -- 'KFG state 1100 leaves the ground mid-move (StateTypeSet, Specials.cns:693) and both it and 1105 end on pos y > -vel y (Specials.cns:776, :895)'
on_land.corpus: corpus/kfg/Specials.cns:692-696 (StateTypeSet at AnimElem 4), :774-777 (the ChangeState to 1101), :893-896 (state 1105's, to state 52)
on_land.derivation: `pos y > -vel y` is `pos_y + vel_y > 0`, i.e. the attacker will be at or below the ground on the next tick, which is the `landing` predicate. The move goes airborne at AnimElem 4 via StateTypeSet stateType = A, physics = N (:692-696), so the motion track and gravity own everything after that tick.
on_land.note: duration_bound is the field that matters here. The shipped [P] recovery of 18 came from the animation length, and the state's REAL length is whatever the trajectory takes. Declaring `lower` asserts the authored number is no longer than reality, which keeps the error permissive. An author who cannot show that must declare `upper` and justify it, because `upper` hides infinites.

transitions.duration_derivation: The [P] recovery of 18 is the animation-length reading (mugen_cns.py:560-561) and the state actually ends on the landing predicate at corpus/kfg/Specials.cns:776. On the authored motion track plus gravity 128 sub/tick the landing tick is at or after the animation end, so the authored duration is a LOWER bound on the real one: the model frees the attacker no later than the game does. PERMISSIVE, therefore safe in ADR-001:224-225's sense. Re-derive when the motion track is transcribed in Phase 3.

invuln_and_freeze.adr_001: section 4 group E, :236-240 -- 'KFG super_palm has per-frame invulnerability by attack attribute: NotHitBy with value = ,NA,SA,AT for 11 ticks from AnimElem 2, value2 = C,NA thereafter (Supers.cns:34-43). Same move needs SuperPause time 30 with poweradd -1000 (Supers.cns:17-23).'
invuln_and_freeze.derivation: AnimElem 2 begins tick 3 and AnimElem 14 begins tick 40 (corpus/kfg/Kung Fu Girl.air:2470 onward). Window A: trigger AnimElem = 2, time = 11, so ticks 3-13, attributes NA/SA/AT with an EMPTY state-type field (the leading comma at :38) meaning all. Window B: trigger AnimElemTime(2) >= 0 && AnimElemTime(14) < 0 with time = 1, i.e. re-armed every tick from 3 until element 14 begins, so ticks 3-39, attribute C,NA. The two OVERLAP rather than abut -- ADR-001:237-238's 'thereafter' is right about which one outlasts the other but the second starts at the same tick as the first.
invuln_and_freeze.note_on_the_superpause: Supers.cns:17-23 authors pos, anim, sound and poweradd and NO `time` parameter, so the 30 ticks ADR-001:239 cites are MUGEN's SuperPause DEFAULT, not a number this character states. ticks_authored: false records that. poweradd -1000 is -100 meter units at 10 power per unit, which is the [P] effect.meter already shipped.

invuln.source: corpus/kfg/Supers.cns:41-45, re-armed every tick with time = 1 until AnimElem 14 at tick 40

hit_condition.adr_001: section 4 group G, :256-260 -- 'Every one of Kung Fu Girl's 17 normals gates its HitDef on trigger1 = !var(16) && var(15) < 1 (Normal.cns:27, byte-identical on the other 16). var(15) counts hits since the defender was last grounded, var(16) flags a hit-fall state (System.cns:2611-2666).'
hit_condition.move: kung_fu_girl.json / stand_lp, and the other 16 normals identically
hit_condition.corpus: corpus/kfg/Normal.cns:27; the same trigger appears at :186 on chop and :776 on stand_hk_far, which is what 'byte-identical' means here
hit_condition.derivation: var(16) is the defender's hit-fall flag and var(15) the count of hits since the defender was last grounded, both authored in corpus/kfg/System.cns:2611-2666. The character disables MUGEN's own juggle system to run them: AssertSpecial nojugglecheck (System.cns:2590-2593) and [Data] airjuggle = 0 (System.cns:7). The rule is 'a normal does not connect against an already-juggled defender'.
hit_condition.note: TWO CLAUSES, BOTH ANDs -- which is why $defs.predicateList is a flat `all` list and not a grammar. This is the shape ADR-002:76-78 says to encode as data so the parser stays deferred. Placed at move level rather than under `engine` because ADR-001:299 and :304 spell it that way and because Phase 5's trigger language is what will read it (field class E5). VERIFIED to be invisible to today's loader in x-v2-verification.

cancel_condition.adr_001: section 4 group G, :262-264 -- 'All 26 AOF2 cancels re-enter from [Statedef 1010] under p2bodydist x <= 30 && p2movetype != H (States.st:190, :197). The second clause literally reads only attack when the defender is not in hitstun -- an explicit, authored anti-combo rule.'

cancel_condition.corpus: corpus/aof2/States.st:186-191 (punk branch) and :193-198 (fat branch), re-read at both
cancel_condition.derivation: The full trigger set on the punk branch is var(0) = 0 || var(0) = 1 (:188), roundstate = 2 && random < 50 (:189), and p2bodydist x <= 30 && p2movetype != H (:190). The first is the variant selector and belongs in engine.variants; the random roll is not encodable in a deterministic simulation and goes in `unmodelled`; the third is the predicate. 30 px * 256 = 7680 sub-units.
cancel_condition.note: ADR-001:191 also carries a THIRD opponent property inside the target selector: value = ifelse((p2statetype != C && random < 333), 1020, ...). All three of the properties ADR-001:270 names for Phase 5 -- p2statetype, p2movetype, p2bodydist -- therefore appear in fourteen lines of one character. Authoring this once on a cancel_families entry rather than 26 times is the intended shape.

condition.unmodelled: The same trigger block carries `roundstate = 2 && random < 50` (States.st:189), evaluated EVERY TICK. A deterministic rollback simulation cannot use MUGEN's random at all and the prover's model has no probability (ADR-001:275-279), so the probability gate is dropped and a sometimes-edge becomes an always-edge. PERMISSIVE: it can invent an infinite, it cannot hide one. ADR-001 section 4 group H is explicit that this is not a trigger-language problem at all -- 'the transition itself is a policy', and ADR-001 section 8 item 5 puts AI selection in a SEPARATE authored artifact rather than in this file.

per_variant_gap_actions.adr_001: section 4 group I, :288-294 -- 'AOF2 is a spawner plus four disjoint sub-characters... Moves and cancels can be duplicated per variant; A gap_action CANNOT -- gap_actions, walk_speed, decay, scaling and resources are character-global.'
per_variant_gap_actions.corpus: corpus/aof2/States.st:232-253 (the run state), :239-242 (punk velset x = 8.5), :244-247 (fat velset x = 5.5), :252 (ends at time >= 20); :71-73 (var(0) = random % 4, rolled once); :5-44 (the root spawns the helper); :1382-1387 (the root is made unhittable)
per_variant_gap_actions.derivation: One run is a fixed 20-tick commitment. Punk: 8.5 * 20 = 170 px = 170 space units (model.py:465-468 makes one space unit exactly one pixel at scale 100 against reach units of 100 px). Fat: 5.5 * 20 = 110. The file today authors ONE action at 170 and documents the over-credit; v2 lets both be written.
per_variant_gap_actions.note: THE UNION IS THE SAFE READING AND IT MUST BE STATED IN notes[] (assertion A11). json_spec.py:168-184 gives the modelled character every gap action, so it may use either run. Each keeps its own frames, effect, guard and max_uses, so no variant's restriction is dropped and the union is at least as permissive as any single variant -- a TERMINATING verdict over the union implies TERMINATING for all four sub-characters, which is the direction AOF2's verdict needs. The cost is that an INFINITE verdict over a multi-variant file may name a route mixing one variant's move with another's gap action, which no single sub-character can perform. Permissive, so safe, but a reader must be told.

variants.prover_reading: The prover sees the UNION of all four variants: json_spec.py:168-184 reads every gap action regardless of its variant tag. Each action keeps its own frames, effect, guard and max_uses, so the union is at least as permissive as any single variant and a TERMINATING verdict over it implies TERMINATING for every sub-character. An INFINITE verdict over it would NOT imply an infinite for any single sub-character, because the search may mix one variant's move with another variant's gap action. Permissive in ADR-001:224-225's sense -- it can invent an infinite, it cannot hide one.

x-v2-where-floats-remain.$comment: ARCHITECTURE.md:47 (D2) requires integers for everything the simulation integrates over time, and ADR-001:311-315 records that D2 'survives, strengthened' because no move needed a float to say what it does. v2 ADDS NO FLOATS. Every field v2 introduces is an integer, in sub-units where it is a distance or a velocity, in hundredths where it is damage, in permille where it is a ratio. The floats below are all inherited from v1 and each has a reason to stay.
x-v2-where-floats-remain.damage: float in both implementations (json_spec.py:69, and Move.damage in model.py). Feeds Result.maxDamage only and never the verdict. The engine's integer original is engine.quantized_sources.damage_hundredths and, per hit, engine.hits[].damage_hundredths.
x-v2-where-floats-remain.reach: float reach units, quantized by the prover itself at model.py:465-468 to hundredths. The engine's integer original is quantized_sources.reach_px; the simulation never reads the float.
x-v2-where-floats-remain.pushback: same as reach, and it is an ESTIMATE regardless of its type (ADR-001:486-494) -- making it an integer would not make it derived.
x-v2-where-floats-remain.walk_speed: float reach units per frame, quantized at model.py:468. ADR-001:499-504 documents the one place this rounds: Kung Fu Man's 2.4 px/tick is 614 sub-units exactly for the engine but lands on 2 px/tick for the prover, losing 0.4. UNDER-states attacker mobility, so it can hide an infinite but not invent one.
x-v2-where-floats-remain.scaling_and_decay_table: float multiplier arrays. Integer permille originals live in quantized_sources.scaling_permille and decay_table_permille. decay.ratio is now dead (see x-v2-changes.narrowings).
x-v2-where-floats-remain.why_they_are_not_converted: Every one of them is a [P] field. Retyping a [P] field would break json_spec.py's float() coercions or change a verdict, and v2's contract is that it changes neither. The integer originals sit beside them in engine.quantized_sources, which is what makes D8 checkable -- ADR-001 section 8 leaves the [P] surface alone deliberately.

The counts 17 and 26 are worth noting -- they were produced by matching on the source data, and they reproduce ADR-001:256 ('all 17 of its normals') and ADR-001:262 ('All 26 AOF2 cancels') independently.

Deleting every key named `engine`, `certain`, `caveat` or `hit_condition` recursively from the v2 demonstration files and re-analysing gives byte-identical output on 3 of 3. The prover subset is 28% / 33% / 16% of each file by bytes. This is what makes the class table above a measurement rather than a claim: nothing v2 adds is visible to the fragment.
x-v2-verification.load_assertions: A01-A13 VERIFIED against all three shipped files and all four demonstration files. A01 (decay.floor <= min hitstun): Kung Fu Girl floor 0 vs 9, Kung Fu Man floor 10 vs 11, AOF2 floor 5 vs 7 -- all pass, Kung Fu Man by one frame. A02: no file uses multiplicative. A03: all seven files declare [meter, juggle] in that order. A04: no file authors __space in a move or cancel map. A05/A07/A09: every hits[0].tick equals its move's startup and every projectile spawn_tick equals its move's startup, on real data.
x-v2-verification.two_defects_this_verification_found_in_t: Recorded because a verification that finds nothing usually means it was not run. (1) `derivation_legend` was drafted as type object, and kung_fu_girl.json ships it as a prose string, so the first superset run FAILED on that file -- the same defect class as the minItems:2 bug ADR-001:541-545 records, a schema tightened past what its own characters author. Now string-or-object. (2) Assertion A06 was drafted without the unconditional-records exclusion and fired on chop, whose two hit profiles are mutually exclusive and can never both land; hitRecord.hitstun_ticks was also optional, which made A06 silently unevaluable on a record that omitted it. Both fixed, and the second is why hitstun_ticks is now required. A third, procedural: `analyse` EXITS 1 WHEN THE VERDICT IS INFINITE, which is the verdict and not a failure -- a first draft of the comparison harness discarded stdout on a non-zero exit and made the Kung Fu Girl comparison pass vacuously. Any CI job that gates on this tool must compare output, not exit status.
x-v2-verification.a_correction_to_ADR_001: ADR-001:496-497 states that hitstun decay is 'Shipped as none for KFG and AOF2... KFM ships the house rule with the floor lowered.' The files say otherwise, and the files are right: kung_fu_girl.json ships kind none, kung_fu_man.json ships linear step 2 floor 10 (the UNMODIFIED house rule), and aof2_strength_training.json ships linear step 2 floor 5 (the LOWERED one, and its own decay.engine.derivation explains at length why 10 would be unsound for it). The two characters are transposed in that sentence. No file is wrong and no verdict is affected -- assertion A01 passes on all three -- but ADR-001 section 6.3's prose should be corrected when it is next touched.
